analysis: The strongest closest response now retains the broad UCR legal sequence and adds actual transnational business law with its formal business foundation, replacing generic persuasion and American-history research. It combines this substantial legal study with political, sociological, economic, ethical and empirical inquiry appropriate to the target’s social-context emphasis.

The sustainability option retains substantial law, adding transnational commercial law, business foundations, public economics and actual public policy. Removed broad farming/geology content, generic data work and an unspecified partner research project whose original legal relevance was overstated. The practice option replaces primary-school rhetorical teaching with AI-governance study; rhetorical communication and negotiation remain bounded complements, while actual legal arbitration supplies practice.

Every course contribution was reconsidered from the active profile or description. The description-only policy course receives full consideration for policy phases and memo work. Economics is not tax/labour-law doctrine, commercial law does not automatically provide company-formation law, and general rhetoric is not court procedure. Twelve partial relationships use actual shared legal subjects or disciplinary methods, with specific gaps in Dutch specialisms, duplicated subjects, the thesis and minor choice. Administrative content within Comparative Constitutional Law is acknowledged without counting it twice.

All seven original offering conflicts are repaired by rescheduling criminal law, economics and AI work or replacing the weak partner-project selection. All three twenty-four-course schedules pass prerequisites, offerings, first-year PPD and advanced-course requirements. Foundations precede dependent legal/business/economic courses, and sustainability foundations precede governance. Every pair passes thirty EC each way and substantive distinctness. Optional research remains with the actual thesis outside scheduled credits.

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.contribution: Academic writing, literature evaluation, civic collaboration and reflective practice provide the first-year common foundation.

BENBUSI211.name: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
BENBUSI211.contribution: examines AI’s economic and institutional implications, regulation, corporate responsibility, labour and inequality through business cases and country research

BENBUSI311.name: Transnational Business Law
BENBUSI311.contribution: examines legal frameworks for cross-border contracts, trade, finance, intellectual property and digital commerce, with advisory assignments and simulated arbitration

BENECON111.name: Introduction to Economics
BENECON111.contribution: introduces economic choice, markets, strategic interaction and government’s economic role as specific foundations for analysing regulation

BENECON212.name: Microeconomics & Behavior
BENECON212.contribution: examines incentives, uncertainty, strategic behaviour, labour/capital markets and externalities as an economic complement to legal regulation

BENECON311.name: Public Economics
BENECON311.contribution: examines public goods, taxation, spending, externalities and redistribution through policy models and research; this is an economic contribution rather than tax-law doctrine

BENENTR312.name: International Business & Governance
BENENTR312.contribution: examines trade, institutions, policy conflict and cross-border business decisions, supporting the international commercial context of legal practice

BENGATE101.name: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations
BENGATE101.contribution: develops business models and the functions of enterprises, providing organisational context and the formal foundation for transnational business law without claiming company-law doctrine

BENGATE102.name: Research Methods & Statistics
BENGATE102.contribution: develops empirical design, measurement, statistics and a data-collection project as a methodological complement to socio-legal inquiry

BENLEAD311.name: Psychology of Organizations & Leadership
BENLEAD311.contribution: examines motivation, leadership, teams, power, conflict and organisational change, including evidence synthesis for organisational cases

BENLEAD312.name: Negotiation & Strategic Thinking
BENLEAD312.contribution: develops bargaining, interests, power, trust and strategic conflict management through negotiation simulations and scenario design

ENSDELT312.name: Governance of Sustainability
ENSDELT312.contribution: examines institutions, power, participation, justice and collective decisions in sustainability, with stakeholder consultation and policy advice/evaluation

ENSGATE101.name: Sustainability Essentials I
ENSGATE101.contribution: introduces planetary boundaries and scientific methods for understanding environmental pressures and sustainability interventions

ENSSUST111.name: Climate Change
ENSSUST111.contribution: examines climate science, impacts, adaptation, mitigation, justice and governance, supplying scientific and social substance for environmental regulation

GOSGATE102.name: Law, Society & Justice
GOSGATE102.contribution: introduces legal traditions, public/private law, justice and social context through case briefs, legal interpretation, mock trials and a socio-legal proposal

GOSLAWJ111.name: Human Rights: Law & Philosophy
GOSLAWJ111.contribution: examines human-rights law, protection institutions, landmark cases and philosophical justifications through legal and normative argument

GOSLAWJ211.name: Criminal Law & Criminal Justice
GOSLAWJ211.contribution: examines criminal liability, punishment, criminalisation, excuses, offences and participation, with legal-advice memoranda and a criminology research proposal

GOSLAWJ212.name: Introduction to Public International Law
GOSLAWJ212.contribution: examines international legal sources, state responsibility, institutions, force, human rights and treaty politics through legal cases and critical research

GOSLAWJ213.name: Comparative Constitutional Law
GOSLAWJ213.contribution: compares constitutional structures, rights, courts and judicial review, with administrative participation, remedies and procedural fairness

GOSLAWJ311.name: Principles of Private Law
GOSLAWJ311.contribution: examines property, tort and contract rights across legal systems through legal briefs, comparative contract research and simulated mediation

GOSLAWJ312.name: Foundations of European Union Law
GOSLAWJ312.contribution: examines EU institutions, competences, legal effect, remedies, citizenship and free movement through current judgments and legal cases

GOSPHIL212.name: Ethics
GOSPHIL212.contribution: develops ethical interpretation, normative argument and independent positions on moral theory and practical questions relevant to legal judgement

GOSPOLI111.name: Introduction to Political Philosophy
GOSPOLI111.contribution: examines political authority, rights, human nature and social order through primary texts and normative argument

GOSPOLI112.name: Foundations of Comparative Politics
GOSPOLI112.contribution: examines democracy, institutions, elections and political actors through empirical comparison, giving concrete political context to constitutional law

GOSPOLI212.name: Theory of International Relations
GOSPOLI212.contribution: examines international relations, conflict and cooperation through theories, cases and a UN simulation, complementing international legal institutions

GOSPOLI311.name: European Union Politics
GOSPOLI311.contribution: examines EU integration, representation, legitimacy and policymaking, including empirical parliamentary research that complements EU legal analysis

GOSPOLI312.name: Public Policy Analysis
GOSPOLI312.contribution: examines policy-making processes and alternative analytical frameworks through a sugar-policy case and policy memos, supporting the legal-governance perspective

GOSPOLI313.name: Peace & Conflict
GOSPOLI313.contribution: examines conflict, humanitarian law, human rights, peacebuilding and transitional justice through interdisciplinary research and a policy brief

GOSSOCI111.name: Introduction to Sociology
GOSSOCI111.contribution: examines social institutions, inequality, identity and boundaries through social theory and evidence, complementing analysis of law’s social context

GOSSOCI212.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
GOSSOCI212.contribution: develops qualitative design, interviews, documentary inquiry, coding and interpretation for empirical investigation of social and institutional questions

GOSSOCI215.name: Social Movements & Environmental Justice
GOSSOCI215.contribution: examines environmental-justice movements, collective action and feminist/anticolonial perspectives through actual environmental cases

GOSSOCI311.name: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
GOSSOCI311.contribution: examines civil society, trust, public spheres, solidarity and social repair through theory and empirical study of an organisation or movement

MCCCOMM111.name: The Art of Rhetorical Communication
MCCCOMM111.contribution: develops rhetorical analysis, argument construction, debating and public speaking; its communication contribution is distinguished from legal procedure

MCCCOMM212.name: Communicating the Climate Crisis
MCCCOMM212.contribution: examines climate communication, public argument and contested policy through media analysis and an intervention in public debate

MCCCOMM311.name: Persuasive Communication
MCCCOMM311.contribution: examines persuasion, framing and ethics through research and community projects, complementing professional communication rather than supplying courtroom training

MCCMEDI212.name: Media & the Environment
MCCMEDI212.contribution: examines representations of ecological risk, scientific knowledge and human–environment relations as forces in public debate and environmental ethics

alignment.rationale: Both examine technology, economic change, institutions and regulation in society. UCR concentrates on AI, firms and economic governance; Tilburg integrates technological, law-and-economics and legal-psychological perspectives.

Both develop legal-source analysis, reasoned written legal advice and oral advocacy in a simulated dispute. UCR uses transnational business arbitration; Tilburg uses Dutch judicial pleadings and procedural documents.

Both address methods of resolving disputes. UCR develops negotiation and bargaining through simulations; Tilburg also provides Dutch civil procedure, hearings and fact-finding. The relationship concerns the dispute-resolution part only.
Both develop legal concepts, legal-source interpretation, reasoning and case analysis, while situating law in a wider social and normative context.

Both examine fundamental rights, their legal and philosophical foundations, and national/international protection. Tilburg additionally concentrates on their operation in the Dutch and EU legal orders.
Both examine legality, causation, intent, guilt, justifications, excuses, attempts and participation as grounds and limits of criminal liability.

Both provide substantive public-international-law study. UCR combines foundational sources and institutions with contemporary legal cases and critical perspectives; the relationship is partial rather than a claim of identical specialist coverage.
Both examine state organisation, legislation, government institutions, rights and constitutional constraints. UCR adopts a comparative approach rather than a dedicated Dutch sequence.
Both examine property, tort and contract concepts, rights and obligations through legal cases. UCR compares multiple legal systems; Tilburg establishes Dutch private-law foundations.
Both examine the EU legal order, effects on national law, citizenship, free movement and legal protection. Tilburg also addresses competition law and procurement.

Both develop normative analysis of moral and social problems. UCR provides ethical theories and argument; Tilburg integrates these questions specifically with positive law and political/legal institutions.

Both examine the EU as a political and institutional union, representation and legitimacy. Tilburg frames these as questions of legal/political philosophy; UCR combines institutional analysis with empirical political research.
No selected course centres European legal history; general historical or political context is not substituted for legal-historical study.
Criminal Law and Criminal Justice has its strongest primary placement with advanced criminal liability. No second course is counted for this combined introductory substantive/procedural course.
Business foundations and transnational commercial law provide context, but no selected course centres Dutch corporation/partnership formation, organisation and termination.
The selected international and EU law courses have stronger primary placements with the dedicated second-year courses and are not counted again.
Comparative Constitutional Law includes administrative principles but is placed with constitutional law; no additional course supplies the dedicated Dutch administrative-law introduction.
Legal and communication skills occur across the UCR options, but no additional course provides the dedicated procedural-document training across criminal, private and administrative law.
Public Economics supplies a complementary analysis of taxation and redistribution, not the substantive Dutch tax-law rules of this course.
Principles of Private Law is placed with the broad private-law introduction; no second course supplies the dedicated Dutch property-law deepening.

Contract content is developed within selected private and business law courses, but their strongest primary placements are the private-law introduction and simulated legal-dispute practice. No course is counted twice.
The selected constitutional/administrative and human-rights courses support parts of the subject, but no separate course develops this dedicated Dutch judicial-protection sequence.
Private Law includes tort and liability but is already placed with the broader introductory course; no second course is counted for dedicated Dutch tort-law study.
Substantive criminal liability and a legal-aid simulation do not reproduce the dedicated Dutch criminal-process sequence.
Comparative methods occur within the UCR legal courses, but no additional course provides this dedicated global legal-traditions sequence.
Economic and organisational courses offer complementary perspectives on work and institutions, but no selected course provides Dutch individual/collective labour-law doctrine.
No compulsory Dutch legal thesis is scheduled at UCR. Optional independent research appears separately outside scheduled credits.
Open minor space remains unspecified; no particular minor or exchange package is invented.
